examples.ko: 불씨가 꺼지지 않게 장작을 더 넣었어요.
examples.en: I added more firewood so the embers would not die out.

examples.ko: 작은 불씨 하나가 큰 산불로 번졌어요.
examples.en: One small ember spread into a big forest fire.

examples.ko: 모닥불의 불씨를 물로 꼭 꺼야 해요.
examples.en: You must put out the embers of the campfire with water.
Grandmother left embers in the fireplace.
Without a lighter it was hard to get a spark going.

examples.ko: 불씨가 아직 살아 있어서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The embers are still alive, so we have to be careful.

explain: 불씨는 꺼지지 않고 남아 있는 작은 불이에요. 튀어 오르는 작은 불덩이는 '불똥'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 비유로 큰 문제를 일으킬 작은 원인에도 써요.

phrases.example: 작은 오해가 큰 싸움의 불씨가 됐어요.
phrases.en: A small misunderstanding became the spark of a big fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 갈등이나 사건이 시작되는 작은 원인을 말할 때 비유로 써요. 싸움, 논란, 갈등과 자주 같이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for the small cause that starts a big conflict or incident. It often appears with fights, controversies and conflicts.

explain_en: 불씨 is a small fire that stays alive and can start a bigger one. '불똥' is different: it is a small flying spark. Figuratively, 불씨 is a small cause that can grow into a big problem.

examples.en: The children draw pictures on the ground with a stick.
Grandfather walks leaning on a stick.
I picked fruit using just one stick.

examples.ko: 텐트를 작대기 몇 개로 받쳐 놓았어요.
examples.en: I propped up the tent with a few poles.
The stick I picked up on the road is quite sturdy.
I tied a string to a stick and made a fishing rod.

explain: '막대기'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 군대에서는 계급장의 줄을 '작대기'라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.en: I poked the ant nest with a stick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 거의 같고 더 널리 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning and the more widely used word.

phrases.en: I picked the persimmon with a long pole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 곳의 물건을 따거나 받칠 때 쓰는 모습이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Natural for reaching something high or propping something up.

phrases.en: The child runs around swinging a stick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막대기를 흔들거나 돌릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for waving or swinging a stick.

explain_en: Long straight stick for leaning on or propping. It is used almost the same as '막대기'. In the military, the stripes on a rank insignia are also called '작대기'.

t90.ax: I picked fruit using just one stick.

examples.en: I stocked up on a lot of ramen during the sale.

examples.ko: 태풍이 온다고 해서 물을 쟁여 놨어요.
examples.en: A typhoon was coming, so I stored up water.
I have a habit of stocking the fridge with side dishes.
Grandmother keeps rice stored up in the shed.

examples.ko: 책을 방에 쟁이면 걸어 다니기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you pile books up in the room, it's hard to walk around.

examples.ko: 좋아하는 과자를 쟁일 수 있어서 기뻐요.
examples.en: I'm happy I can stock up on my favorite snacks.

explain: '쌓다'는 위로 높이 올리는 것이고, '쟁이다'는 나중에 쓰려고 많이 모아 두는 것이에요. 말할 때는 '쟁여 두다', '쟁여 놓다'로 많이 쓰고, 할인할 때 사 두는 것을 '쟁이다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I stocked up on kimchi to eat in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쟁이다'에 '두다'를 붙여 '모아 둔 상태'를 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 두다 emphasizes the stocked-up state.

phrases.en: I stocked up on snacks during the sale.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잔뜩'은 아주 많이라는 뜻이라 많이 사 둘 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: 잔뜩 means 'a whole lot', fitting for buying large amounts.

phrases.example: 집이 좁으니까 물건을 너무 쟁이지 마세요.
phrases.en: Our home is small, so please don't stockpile too many things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령형으로 써서 너무 많이 사 두지 말라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command telling someone not to hoard too much.

explain_en: '쌓다' is stacking things up high; '쟁이다' is stockpiling a lot for later use. In speech it's usually '쟁여 두다' or '쟁여 놓다', and also for buying extra on sale.

examples.en: My uncle got his high school diploma through an equivalency exam.

examples.ko: 검정고시는 일 년에 두 번 있어요.
examples.en: The equivalency exam is held twice a year.
She prepared for the equivalency exam while working.

examples.ko: 검정고시에 합격해서 대학에 갈 수 있게 됐어요.
examples.en: I passed the equivalency exam, so I could go to university.

examples.ko: 나이가 많아도 검정고시는 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can take the equivalency exam even if you are older.

examples.ko: 검정고시 학원에는 다양한 나이의 사람들이 다녀요.
examples.en: People of many ages attend the equivalency exam academy.

explain: 학교를 다니지 못했거나 중간에 그만둔 사람이 초등학교·중학교·고등학교 졸업 자격을 얻는 시험이에요. 보통 '검정고시를 보다', '검정고시에 합격하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I will take the equivalency exam next spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험을 치른다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say you take this exam.

phrases.en: My older brother passed the equivalency exam and went to university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험에 붙었다는 뜻이에요. 조사 '에'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you passed the exam. The particle 에 is used.

phrases.en: I go to an equivalency exam academy in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 시험을 준비하는 학원을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a cram school that prepares students for this exam.

explain_en: This is the exam people take when they missed or left school and still want an elementary, middle or high school graduation qualification. The usual verbs are 검정고시를 보다 and 검정고시에 합격하다.

examples.en: While driving at night, I saw a water deer on the road.
In the countryside, water deer come down into the fields.

examples.ko: 고라니 울음소리가 무서워서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The water deer's cry was so scary that I couldn't sleep.
A water deer jumped out in front of the car on the mountain road.
A water deer looks like a deer but has no antlers.
The farmers worry a lot because of water deer.

explain: 사슴과 비슷하게 생겼지만 다른 동물이에요. 시골길이나 논밭 이야기, 도로에서 차에 치이는 '로드킬' 뉴스에 나오기도 해요.

phrases.en: A water deer suddenly appeared on the mountain road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운전이나 산책 중에 만난 상황에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits meeting one while driving or walking.

phrases.en: I was startled by a water deer's cry at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시골의 밤 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in stories about the countryside at night.

phrases.example: 차 앞으로 고라니가 튀어나와서 급하게 멈췄어요.
phrases.en: A water deer sprang out in front of the car, so I stopped suddenly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 나타나 놀란 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it appears suddenly and surprises you.

explain_en: It looks like a deer but is a different animal. It comes up in stories about country roads and fields, and in news about roadkill.

en: to adhere; to defend; to keep

examples.ko: 그 식당은 십 년 동안 같은 맛을 고수했어요.
examples.en: That restaurant stuck to the same taste for ten years.
The boss holds on to his opinion to the end.
If you only stick to the old way, it's hard to improve.
To keep the price, they didn't offer discounts.

examples.ko: 그는 처음 약속한 입장을 고수하고 있어요.
examples.en: He is holding to the position he first promised.

examples.ko: 무조건 고수하지 말고 다른 방법도 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't just insist no matter what; think of other ways too.

explain: '지키다'와 비슷하지만 의견, 입장, 방식을 바꾸지 않고 버틴다는 느낌이 강해요. 좋게 쓸 수도 있고 고집을 비판할 때도 써요. 바둑 '고수'와는 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: He held to his position to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이나 태도를 바꾸지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone won't change their view or attitude.

phrases.en: This bakery sticks to the old method.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래된 방법을 그대로 지킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when keeping an old method as it is.

phrases.en: My father always insists on the same route.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하지만 더 일상적이고 '고집'이 센 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but more everyday and stresses stubbornness.

explain_en: It is close to '지키다', but it carries a stronger sense of holding firm to an opinion, position or method without changing. It can be positive or critical of stubbornness. It is a different word from '고수' in Go, which only sounds the same.

examples.en: My mother likes precious metals like gold rings.
I ordered wedding rings at a jewelry shop.

examples.ko: 귀금속은 값이 비싸서 잘 보관해야 해요.
examples.en: Precious metals are expensive, so they must be stored well.
A thief stole jewelry from the house.
Gold and silver are typical precious metals.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때는 귀금속을 많이 가져가지 않아요.
examples.en: I do not bring much jewelry when I travel.

explain: 금, 은, 백금처럼 값이 많이 나가는 금속과 그것으로 만든 장신구를 같이 부를 때 써요. 값싼 '액세서리'와는 느낌이 달라요. 가게 간판에는 '귀금속'이나 '금은방'이 많이 붙어 있어요.

phrases.en: I bought a necklace at a jewelry store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금이나 은 장신구를 파는 가게를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shop selling gold or silver jewelry.

phrases.en: I gave my wife fine jewelry as an anniversary gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금이나 은으로 만든 값진 장신구를 선물할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when giving valuable jewelry made of gold or silver as a gift.
phrases.en_equiv: give fine jewelry as a gift

phrases.en: Gold prices went up, so precious-metal prices rose too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금, 은 같은 금속의 값 이야기를 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the price of metals like gold and silver.

explain_en: It covers valuable metals like gold, silver, and platinum, plus jewelry made from them. It feels different from cheap '액세서리'. Shop signs often say '귀금속' or '금은방'.

examples.en: I met the final boss in the last stage of the game.
You need a lot of practice to reach the final stage.

examples.ko: 축구 경기 끝판에 골이 두 개나 나왔어요.
examples.en: Two goals came in the final stretch of the soccer game.
As the end drew near, everyone got nervous.
The last stage is always the hardest.
I felt great after clearing the last stage.

explain: 경기, 게임, 일에서 마지막 단계나 마지막 무렵을 가리켜요. '마지막'보다 입말에 가깝고 가벼워요. 비슷한 '막판'은 승부가 갈리는 마지막 순간에 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The final boss of this game is really strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임의 마지막 적을 말하고, 어떤 분야에서 가장 센 것을 비유하기도 해요. 예: 매운맛의 끝판왕.
phrases.nuance_en: The last enemy in a game; also figuratively the ultimate in some field, as in the final boss of spicy food.

explain_en: It refers to the last stage or last stretch of a match, game, or task. It is more spoken and casual than 마지막. The similar 막판 fits better for the final moment when a result is decided.

t90.ax: The last stage is always the hardest.

examples.en: It's cold, and on top of that, the wind is blowing too.

examples.ko: 몸도 안 좋은데 더더구나 일까지 많아요.
examples.en: I don't feel well, and on top of that I have a lot of work.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 비싸고 더더구나 색도 마음에 안 들어요.
examples.en: This outfit is expensive, and moreover I don't even like the color.

examples.ko: 저는 요리를 못하는데 더더구나 오늘은 재료도 없어요.
examples.en: I'm bad at cooking, and what's more, I have no ingredients today.

examples.ko: 길도 막히고 더더구나 비까지 와서 늦었어요.
examples.en: The roads were jammed, and on top of that it rained, so I was late.

examples.ko: 더더구나 이렇게 늦은 시간에는 갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Especially at such a late hour, I can't go.

explain: '더구나'를 더 힘주어 말하는 느낌이에요. 앞의 이야기에 더해서 상황이 더 심해지거나 더 그렇다는 걸 덧붙일 때 써요. 말할 때는 '게다가'나 '더구나'로 바꿔도 돼요.

phrases.en: The traffic is bad, and what's more, it's raining.
phrases.nuance_ko: '더더구나'보다 덜 힘주어 말하는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic, less emphatic version of '더더구나'.

phrases.en: The food is delicious, and besides, it's cheap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural choice in everyday speech.

phrases.en: I'm sick, and moreover the exam is close.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 조금 격식 있는 말에서 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits writing or slightly formal speech.

explain_en: It feels like a more emphatic version of '더구나'. Use it to add that, on top of what you just said, the situation is even more so. In speech you can swap it for '게다가' or '더구나'.

t90.ax: Especially at such a late hour, I can't go.

examples.en: A vine is growing along the fence.
I rested for a while under the grapevine.
The vine wraps around the tree and climbs up.
Small pumpkins grew on the pumpkin vine.
A rose vine covered the wall.

examples.ko: 덩굴을 자르지 않으면 집을 다 덮어요.
examples.en: If you don't cut the vine, it will cover the whole house.

explain: 포도, 호박, 장미처럼 줄기가 길게 뻗거나 다른 것을 감고 자라는 식물에 써요. '덩굴'과 '넝쿨'은 둘 다 표준어예요. '덩쿨'은 틀린 표기라서 조심하세요.

phrases.en: The wall is full of vines.
phrases.nuance_ko: '덩굴'과 같은 뜻이고 둘 다 표준어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 덩굴, and both are standard forms.

phrases.en: Vine plants climb up along the fence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄기가 길게 뻗는 식물을 한꺼번에 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A general term for plants with long, climbing stems.

phrases.en: The pumpkin vine stretched all the way to the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 식물의 덩굴인지 앞에 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the plant name before it to say which plant's vine it is.

explain_en: It is used for plants like grapes, pumpkins and roses whose stems stretch long or wind around other things. Both '덩굴' and '넝쿨' are standard words. '덩쿨' is a wrong spelling, so watch out.

examples.en: I heard a woodpecker in the forest.
A woodpecker is pecking at a tree.
Woodpeckers make holes in trees with their beaks.

examples.ko: 산에서 딱따구리를 직접 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever seen a woodpecker in person in the mountains?
A woodpecker's beak is very hard.

examples.ko: 딱따구리가 만든 구멍에 다른 새가 살기도 해요.
examples.en: Sometimes other birds live in holes made by woodpeckers.

explain: 나무를 쪼아 구멍을 내는 새예요. 철자를 '딱다구리'로 잘못 쓰기 쉬운데 표준어는 '딱따구리'예요.

phrases.en: I woke up to the sound of a woodpecker in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '딱따구리'와 '소리'를 붙여 새가 나무를 쪼는 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the sound of a woodpecker pecking at a tree.

phrases.example: 나무 위에 딱따구리 한 마리가 앉아 있어요.
phrases.en: A woodpecker is sitting on the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새를 셀 때는 '한 마리, 두 마리'처럼 '마리'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Animals are counted with the counter '마리', as in one bird, two birds.

phrases.en: The woodpecker pecked the tree and made a hole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딱따구리가 하는 가장 대표적인 행동을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical action associated with a woodpecker.

explain_en: It is a bird that pecks holes in trees. People often misspell it as '딱다구리', but the standard form is '딱따구리'.

examples.en: We take a mock exam at school tomorrow.
My mock test score went up from last month.
I checked my skills with a Korean mock test.

examples.ko: 모의고사는 진짜 시험처럼 시간을 재서 풀어요.
examples.en: You solve a mock test with a timer, like the real exam.

examples.ko: 모의고사가 끝나고 친구들과 답을 맞춰 봤어요.
examples.en: After the mock test, I compared answers with friends.

examples.ko: 고3 학생들은 수능 전에 모의고사를 여러 번 봐요.
examples.en: Third-year high school students take mock tests several times before the CSAT.

explain: 진짜 시험을 미리 연습하는 시험이에요. 한국 고등학생은 대학 시험을 준비하며 '모의고사'를 자주 봐요. 그냥 시험 연습은 '연습 문제'나 '시험 연습'이라고 하고, '모의고사'는 시험 형식을 그대로 따라 한 시험이에요.

phrases.en: I take a mock test every Saturday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험은 '보다'와 같이 쓰는 것이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Exams naturally pair with the verb 보다.

phrases.en: My mock test score went up a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 결과를 말할 때 자주 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to talk about test results.

phrases.en: I have a mock exam tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 '모의고사'는 학교 시험에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but 모의고사 is more common for school exams.

explain_en: A practice exam that copies the real one. Korean high school students take many '모의고사' while preparing for the college entrance exam. Ordinary practice questions are '연습 문제'; a '모의고사' follows the real test format.

en: to defy; to disobey; to rebel

examples.en: Teenagers sometimes rebel against their parents.
That child defied the teacher.
The mother is worried because of her defiant son.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때 이유 없이 반항했어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I rebelled for no reason.
I thought it was useless to rebel.
It's a movie where the main character rebels against society.

explain: '부모님께 반항하다', '선생님께 반항하다'처럼 윗사람의 말을 따르지 않고 맞서는 일에 써요. '반대하다'는 의견이 다르다는 뜻이고, '반항하다'는 태도나 행동으로 대드는 느낌이 더 강해요. 같은 뜻의 명사 '반항'은 '반항기'처럼 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: That child is very defiant these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 말을 안 듣고 대드는 성격이나 태도를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a defiant attitude or personality.

phrases.en: My younger brother talked back to Mom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 행동으로 윗사람에게 맞설 때 쓰는 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual word for confronting an elder in words or actions.

phrases.en: Rebellious feelings grow during puberty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반항하고 싶은 마음을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the urge to rebel.

explain_en: It is used for pushing back against authority, as in 부모님께 반항하다. 반대하다 only means disagreeing, whereas 반항하다 is more about attitude and behavior that talks back. The noun 반항 also appears in words like 반항기 (rebellious phase).

examples.en: Around dawn today the rain suddenly stopped.
When dawn came, the weather turned chilly.
We reached the mountain top around daybreak.

examples.ko: 새벽녘까지 시험 공부를 하느라 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I studied for the exam until dawn and couldn't sleep.
The streets at daybreak are quiet and clear.
I woke up around dawn and opened the window.

explain: '새벽'은 시간대 전체를 말하고, '새벽녘'은 날이 밝아 올 무렵을 가리켜요. '새벽녘에'처럼 때를 나타낼 때 많이 써요. 비슷한 모양의 '해 질 녘'은 해가 질 무렵이에요.

phrases.en: I woke up around daybreak and looked out the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에'를 붙여서 때를 나타내는 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, with 에 marking the time.

phrases.en: I talked with my friend until dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밤새 무언가를 한 뒤 날이 밝아 올 때까지라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means continuing through the night until it gets light.

phrases.en: The streets at dawn are quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여서 그 시간의 모습을 꾸며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 의, it describes the scene at that time.

explain_en: '새벽' covers the whole early-morning period, while '새벽녘' points to the time when day is about to break. It is used in the form '새벽녘에' to say when something happened. The similar '해 질 녘' means around sunset.
